hints.S07_A1: The comparison is with a ripe TOMATO, and the face is FLUSHED WITH COLOUR from the EFFORT and the HEAT. Ask: what colour does skin turn after running hard - paler, calmer, cooler, or the colour of that tomato?
hints.S07_A2: The team was LOSING BY THREE GOALS, yet the coach still wanted them TO KEEP TRYING. Ask: would a good coach scold, punish or ignore his players at that moment, or pour courage into them? Match the verb to his purpose.
hints.S07_A3: She has just won the GOLD MEDAL, so the TEARS OF JOY are already rising and must be kept in. Ask: does 'put off' (delay), 'run away' or 'break down' fit tears? A phrasal verb must be learnt as one whole unit.
hints.S07_A4: The UNDERDOG team scored in the LAST MINUTE and NO ONE COULD BELIEVE IT. Ask: does the idiom describe wild happiness, or illness, trouble, or confusion? An idiom cannot be worked out word by word.
hints.S07_A5: They trained EVERY SINGLE DAY for the CHAMPIONSHIP, so the blank names their very best level. Ask: would anyone train that hard to reach their laziest, weakest or usual performance? Choose the word meaning 'highest point'.
hints.S07_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not the SWIMMING CLUB. Words like nobody and everyone act like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S07_B2: HAS is already in the sentence, so the blank must be its partner. Ask: after has, do we use the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? WIN is irregular, so its participle is not made with -ed.
hints.S07_B3: The STRIKER KICKED it - a sudden action that cut across what the goalkeeper had already begun. Ask: which form shows an action IN PROGRESS in the past? A plain past verb would only show a finished action.
hints.S07_B4: THAN tells you two venues are being compared, and the adjective is long. Ask: do long adjectives take -er, or a helper word in front? 'Usefuler' is not English, and 'most' is for a group of three or above.
hints.S07_B5: The referee BLEW the whistle - a finished past action - and the players reacted IMMEDIATELY. Ask: should the second verb sit in that same finished past, or drift into the present? Both verbs share one time frame.
hints.S07_B6: A tag mirrors the main verb, and the statement uses IS ('Regular exercise IS one of the best ways'). Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag stay positive or turn negative? Keep the same verb - do not borrow 'do'.
hints.S07_B7: TRAINED VERY HARD is a positive effort, yet DID NOT WIN THE TROPHY is a disappointing result. Ask: does this need a reason word like 'because', a result word like 'so', or a word that signals a surprise? Two clashing ideas need a contrast link.
hints.S07_B8: Look at the noun straight after the blank: PLAYERS - many, not one. And the match WAS CANCELLED, so the time is past. Ask: does a plural noun take the singular past verb, or its plural partner? Never match the verb to 'enough'.
hints.S07_C1: The verb in front of the blank is ENJOYS. Ask: after enjoy, can the next verb ever carry 'to', or must it wear the -ing ending? Try each box word in the gap and listen - only one shape may follow enjoy.
hints.S07_C2: EACH DAY WITHOUT FAIL signals a habit, so the tense is simple present - not past, and not this very moment. Ask: HE is one person, so does the present verb stay plain, or does it need -s on the end?
hints.S07_C3: LAST TUESDAY is finished time, so the action is over and done. Ask: is this verb regular? Its past form does not take -ed at all, and 'runned' is not a word. Irregular verbs change their vowel instead.
hints.S07_C4: WHILE tells you the action was already going on when he SPOTTED Mr Lim. Ask: which past form shows an action in progress? And is HE one person or many? That decides whether the helping verb is singular or plural.
hints.S07_C5: The subject is SEVERAL OTHER STUDENTS - more than one, and they are in the middle of moving at that same moment. Ask: which helping verb belongs to a plural subject in the past, and which to one person? Then add the -ing form.
hints.S07_C6: TRIED is followed by an infinitive: he attempted the action on purpose. Ask: which box word carries the little marker that shows an infinitive? The -ing form has already been claimed by ENJOYS at the start of the passage.
hints.S07_C7: SHOULD is a modal verb, like must, can and will. Ask: after a modal, does the verb ever carry -s, -ing or 'to'? Pick the plainest shape in the box - the one a dictionary would list.
hints.S07_C8: RIGHT NOW means at this very moment, as we speak. Ask: does a habit tense fit that, or a tense that shows the action still unfolding? HIS COUSIN is one person, so choose the singular helping verb.
hints.S07_D1: They FILLED THE STANDS and cheer loudly for their FAVOURITE TEAMS. Ask: which box word names the people who WATCH a game rather than play in it? A coach and a referee are never counted in thousands.
hints.S07_D2: Mind the time: this happened IN THE SAME FINAL LAST YEAR, not today - our team actually WON THE MATCH this time. Ask: which box word means 'beaten by the other team'? After HAD BEEN, only a past participle fits.
hints.S07_D3: CALM BUT warns you the next word must contrast with calm, and Reza tells the team to KEEP FIGHTING. Ask: which box word describes someone who has firmly decided to succeed? It must describe a person, so 'coach' cannot fit.
hints.S07_D4: The clue comes right after the blank: he TWISTED HIS ANKLE. Ask: which box word describes a player who has been hurt during play? 'Got' plus this word tells you what happened to his body.
hints.S07_D5: He HELD UP THE TROPHY after the team WON THE MATCH, so the blank names the title they earned. Ask: is Reza the school's coach or referee, or the winner of the whole competition? Choose the word for the top prize-winner.
hints.S07_E1: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about the EXCITEMENT reaching your ears. Ask: which of the two look-alikes has the word EAR hidden inside it? They sound the same, so choose by meaning.
hints.S07_E2: HOLDED forces the regular -ed rule onto a verb that refuses it. Ask: how would you say it about yesterday? Think of sell becoming sold and tell becoming told - the vowel changes instead of an ending being added.
hints.S07_E3: RUNNED is not a word: the -ed rule has been pushed onto an irregular verb. Ask: how do you say it about yesterday? Think of swim becoming swam, and begin becoming began - the vowel does the work.
hints.S07_E4: Everything around it is past: this was LAST SATURDAY, and WE HAD TO RESTART. Ask: is DROP a past form, or the plain base verb? And in a short word ending in one vowel + one consonant, what happens to that last letter before -ed?
hints.S07_E5: The RESULTS SHEET belongs to the COORDINATORS - more than one person. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? When the owners are many, where must the apostrophe go?
hints.S07_F1: The COACH ASKED a yes/no QUESTION and you must now report it. Ask: which small joining word follows asked? Does the reported part keep question order, or normal statement order? And what must 'you' and 'did' become?
hints.S07_F2: One action was already going on; the other one cut across it. Ask: which sentence is the long background action, and which is the sudden event? WHEN goes in front of the sudden one - and never drop the helping verb of the ongoing action.
